newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Chinese vice-premier sticks to Israel schedule.
newsitem.headline: Chinese vice-premier sticks to Israel schedule.

text.p: Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanqing is not interrupting his trip to Israel over the health of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, the China's embassy in Israel said on Tuesday.
"He is still in Israel. He will leave on the 21st (of February) as scheduled," an embassy spokesman told Reuters.
China on Tuesday played down fears over Deng's health raised after Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin cut short an out-of-town trip to visit the ailing patriarch.

"There has been no big change in Comrade Deng Xiaoping's health," Foreign Ministry spokesman Tang Guoqiang told a news briefing, but gave no details of what would constitute a major change in the health of the fragile 92-year-old patriach.
Tang declined to comment when asked if there had been a small change.
Chinese sources said on Monday the Communist party chief and Premier Li Peng both cut short out-of-town trips last weekend to return to Beijing to visit Deng.
